text:
Sam: Figma link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz — uploaded a new iteration for the vectors preview + batch export modal. Two quick asks: keyboard navigation between preview cards and table rows, and a review of the CSV export headers (we need metadata columns). Can people skim for a11y + copy? Maria: :eyes: Looked through — big +1 on showing dims and allowing toggle for 'Show vector dims' (default off). Small copy thing: rename 'Similarity' column to 'Relevance score' and show 3 decimals. Also the export modal CTA should read 'Export vectors (.csv)' not just 'Export'. Kevin: From infra perspective: exporting can be huge. For batches > 5k rows we should trigger an async export job with a link emailed or available in the UI. Streaming CSV from the browser will time out. Backend work needed but straightforward. Freezing the first column (id) is fine; sticky headers doable. Anya: A11y notes: modal needs role="dialog" + aria-modal="true" and focus must move to the modal heading on open. For the export job, use an aria-live="polite" region to announce status updates (e.g., 'Export queued', 'Export ready: 3,200 rows'). Also ensure keyboard users can open a preview card and then tab into the table without losing context. Oliver: Devex nit: empty-state copy for preview should prompt 'Upload a CSV to start mapping' -> prefer 'Upload a .csv to map your columns and preview vectors'. Tooltips: the vector-dim count should be announced on hover AND via aria-label on the toggle button. Maria: On the relevance column: can we make it sortable and show a mini histogram in the header? Could be useful, but probably a next-iteration feature. For now: sort + column width default narrower. Kevin: Sorting server-side for large tables is necessary. For preview (first 100 rows) client-side sort is fine. We'll implement server-side sort for full exports. Also: include a column 'original_text' in export and a 'source_filename' when available. Sam: example CSV header suggestion (quick): ``` vector_id,original_text,relevance_score,vector_dims,source_filename,timestamp ``` Thoughts? Anya: That header looks good. For screen readers, include an additional metadata row? I'd prefer not. Instead ensure column headers have clear aria-labels (e.g., 'Relevance score, sortable'). Kevin: OK to include those columns. We'll cap the export row payload size and add a warning in the modal: 'Exporting more than 10,000 rows may take several minutes — you will be notified when ready.' Maria: UX for keyboard navigation: when a user focuses a preview card and hits Enter, open the detail panel. Focus goes to panel heading, ESC closes and returns focus to the card. Also arrow keys inside the table should move between cells, but Tab still moves by interactive elements. Anya: Quick aria snippet for the export progress region I recommend adding: ```html
Export queued
``` And for the download link: add aria-describedby pointing to file-size and row-count. Oliver: Copy tweak for modal footer: change 'We'll email you when it's ready' -> 'We will notify you here and by email when your export is ready.' more explicit. Sam: Decision summary: 1) Rename 'Similarity' -> 'Relevance score' (3 decimals). 2) Add vector dims toggle + announce dims. 3) CSV header: include original_text and source_filename. 4) Async export job for >5k rows + warning copy for >10k. 5) Modal a11y: role/dialog, focus management, aria-live for export updates. 6) Keyboard nav: Enter to open preview panel, ESC to return, arrow keys to navigate cells. Maria: I'll update the Figma and add the export copy + warning. Kevin: I'll scope backend job + server-side sort. ETA: end of next week. Anya: I'll run a quick keyboard + screen reader pass once Figma updates land. Oliver: I'll patch the empty-state copy and tooltips. design-bot: Uploaded new frames to the Figma link and added comments on the export modal (frame 12). Sam: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll file the small tickets and link them here. Action items: Maria (Figma), Kevin (backend), Anya (a11y review), Oliver (copy). Target: Friday review. Kevin: ack. Maria: ack. Anya: ack. Oliver: ack.
